description: Breaks an MPX note stream back out into seven ordinary signals, allocating the notes across a set number of voices

params.text: Sets how many voices the notes are shared between, 1 to 16, which is also the channel count of every output; left-click the readout for a list of its values, or roll the scroll wheel over it
Chooses what happens to a note that arrives with every voice busy: take the oldest, take the quietest, ignore it, glide within one voice, or play legato across two
Sets how long a glide takes, 0 to 2 seconds, and applies only in the two modes that reuse a sounding voice

inputs.text: Takes the note stream from an MPX output; it carries no voltage, so nothing else can be patched here usefully
Tells this module which voices are sounding, so a voice whose envelope has not finished is not taken for a new note

outputs.text: Carries a gate per voice for as long as that note lasts
Carries the pitch of each voice with any bend already added, so it can be patched straight to an oscillator
Carries the level each note was given, per voice
Carries the bend of each voice on its own, scaled by the bend range that travelled with the note
Carries pressure per voice, and stays where it was for a note whose source sent none
Carries timbre per voice, and stays where it was for a note whose source sent none
Carries the stereo placing of each voice

notes: every output is polyphonic with one channel per voice, so the voice count sets the channel count on all seven at once
mpx IN takes a note stream from the mpx OUT of another DreamerMPX module and from nothing else; with nothing patched there every output stays where it was
this is the module that turns a note stream back into ordinary voltages, and toMPX is the one at the other end that turns voltages into a stream
only one MPX cable is read here; the first one that carries a stream is the one used
a cable between two MPX jacks turns pink once it has taken; a cable from an MPX jack to anything else keeps its ordinary colour and carries nothing
the input takes a cable from an MPX output; an ordinary voltage patched there is not a note stream and nothing comes out
the voice-count plate opens a list of 1 to 16 when it is clicked, and the scroll wheel steps it
an MPX cable carries a note stream rather than a voltage and goes to an MPX input; fromMPX turns a stream back into gates and pitch for the wider rack
